claims.text: Elemental Cr coatings efficiently passivate zirconium-alloy cladding under subcritical-water conditions.
Elemental Cr coatings on zirconium-alloy cladding suffer premature failure in high-temperature steam.
High-temperature Cr–Zr interdiffusion causes the premature failure of elemental Cr coatings on zirconium-alloy cladding.
A thin interfacial ceramic layer such as Al2O3 can act as a diffusion barrier between zirconium alloy and elemental Cr.
The ceramic barrier will impede interfacial Cr–Zr transport.
Limiting elevated-temperature interdiffusion will retard the formation of detrimental intermetallic phases.
Limiting elevated-temperature interdiffusion will retard the formation or growth of detrimental oxide scales.
Retarding interdiffusion and detrimental phase or scale formation will preserve the Cr coating's protective properties.
Retarding interdiffusion and detrimental phase or scale formation will preserve the Cr coating's mechanical integrity.
Barrier-modified samples will exhibit less Cr–Zr interdiffusion than Cr-coated samples without a barrier.
Barrier-modified samples will exhibit less oxide-layer growth than Cr-coated samples without a barrier.
Barrier-modified samples will have greater coating durability than Cr-coated samples without a barrier.
The ceramic-barrier intervention will preserve oxidation resistance and structural integrity in both subcritical water and accident-relevant high-temperature steam.
The proposed intervention is applicable to high-temperature steam exposures above 1000 degrees Celsius.
The proposed intervention is applicable to exposures lasting on the order of hours.
